speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly which antibiotic you were taking, when you started it, and when these symptoms first appeared? I also need to know if you have any known allergies or if you've taken this medication before.

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the joints visibly swollen, warm, or red, or is the pain without any visible inflammation? Also, have you noticed any changes in her urine, such as blood or dark color, or any abdominal pain?

speaker: Doctor
text: Does she have any swelling around the eyes or on her lower legs, and has she experienced any abdominal cramping or vomiting? I need to check if these symptoms suggest a systemic vasculitis triggered by the recent infection.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diagnosed with acute sinusitis one week ago, no known history of adverse drug reactions, immunizations up to date. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash blanch when you press on it, or does it remain red? I also need to know if she has had any abdominal pain or changes in her urine output.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of recent infection followed by rash and joint pain, I need to rule out IgA vasculitis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis.
